subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency requirements (Finly)
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Kyle Barnes <kyle@finly.com>, Priya Shah <priya@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency requirements (Finly)

Hi Kyle / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so the team is aligned and we have clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points you called out:
- p95 latency spikes on peak hours impacting streaming UX (chat responses stutter for some sessions).
- Backend overloaded when concurrent live sessions exceed ~120, causing request queueing and token timeouts.
- Existing solution has poor prefix/KV cache utilization for multi-turn streaming which increases cost.

Current stack + constraints:
- Inference runs on GCP A2 instances behind an internal autoscaler; model is a 13B open model (quantized) with a custom prompt pipeline.
- Synchronous streaming endpoint used by web chat; server-side batching is minimal.
- Compliance: data residency in us-east1, audit logs required for critical flows.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- p95 single-turn inference latency < 250ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) under expected production concurrency.
- Stable streaming tail latency (per-chunk) with p95 < 150ms for interactive chat.
- Support sustained 200 QPS with room to burst to 350 QPS during campaign peaks.
- Clear cost estimate and confidence in fallbacks (smaller model or cached responses) without major UX regressions.

Notes on measurements we requested / you offered:
- You’ll share perf traces from last ramp (attached: finly_latency_traces.tar.gz) and a short sample dataset of typical prompts.
- We’ll run a small proof-of-concept in a dedicated environment to validate p95 and streaming behavior (no production data needed).

Proposed next steps / owners:
1) Finly: share the perf traces + typical prompt corpus (Kyle) — target: EOD Thu 10/22.
2) Redwood: set up a short PoC config (dedicated test pool, streaming-enabled) and run a baseline perf sweep. Deliverable: p95 and streaming tail report + configuration recommendations (Michael / Marissa) — ETA: Tue 10/27.
3) Joint: 30m follow-up to review results and trade-offs (canary plan, quantization, batching tweaks) — propose Wed 10/28 09:30 PT.

Attachments: finly_latency_traces.tar.gz (included in your email), I’ll also attach our baseline SLA playbook after we provision the PoC.

Thanks — looking forward to the traces.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[m] 415-555-0198
From: Kyle Barnes <kyle@finly.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@finly.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 17:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency requirements (Finly)

Thanks Michael — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The 250ms p95 goal applies to single-turn assist queries (user prompt -> single completion) only; multi-turn conversations have slightly higher acceptable tails but streaming chunk latency is what’s hurting UX.
- Our production concurrency baseline is currently 120 sustained concurrent chat sessions. The 200 QPS number is what we need for our planned marketing campaign; we typically see bursts up to 320 for short windows.
- The traces I attached include a 2-hour window from last Monday where the queueing happened (finly_latency_traces.tar.gz). The traces include nginx timelines, app-server logs, and sampled inference latencies.

Questions for Redwood: 
- Can you confirm whether the PoC will include KV/prefix caching so we can see multi-turn improvements?
- Do you have suggested config for streaming chunk sizes — we’re seeing lots of 1-2 token chunks from the current pipeline.

I’ll confirm the dataset share with Priya; we should be able to send a scrubbed sample by EOD Thu.

—Kyle
Kyle Barnes
Head of Product Engineering | Finly
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Kyle Barnes <kyle@finly.com>, Priya Shah <priya@finly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency requirements (Finly)

Appreciate the details, Kyle — helpful. Quick answers and next steps: 
- Yes: PoC will enable prefix/KV caching and a streaming-optimized path so we can measure multi-turn tail improvements. We’ll provide two runs: caching off (baseline) and caching on (optimized).
- Streaming chunk recommendation: start at 16-token chunk target (or buffer 50–100ms) to avoid pathological 1–2 token emissions; we’ll include a tuning matrix in the report.

We’ll provision the PoC in your us-east1-equivalent region and share access instructions. Expect our initial perf sweep (cold and warm cache) with the metrics you care about: p50/p95/p99 single-turn latency, per-chunk tail latency, throughput (QPS), and resource utilization.

Can we lock the follow-up for Wed 10/28 at 09:30 PT? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

I’m attaching the Redwood SLA playbook we’ll use to map results to recommendations (redwood_playbook_sla.pdf).

Best,
Michael
From: Kyle Barnes <kyle@finly.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@finly.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:14:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency requirements (Finly)

Sounds good — Wed 10/28 09:30 PT works for us.
Couple extra data points so the PoC is representative: 
- Sustained concurrency target: 200 QPS (expected steady state).
- Burst target: 350 QPS for ~5–10 minute windows.
- Target single-turn p95: < 250ms (we’ll flag failures > 500ms).
- Streaming per-chunk p95 target: < 150ms.

I’ll forward the scrubbed prompt set and credentials for a test bucket by Thu. Thanks for the rapid turnaround.

—Kyle
